title: Learning to Watermark in the Latent Space of Generative Models
claim: Train a post-hoc watermarker in the latent space, then distill it into the generative model for in-model watermarking.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, lock/unlock icons mark frozen vs trained modules
description: Two horizontal rows separated by a thin line. The top row, 'Train latent watermarker', runs left to right. A painting passes through an encoder E and becomes a latent cube. A red dashed, unlocked embedder 'Emb.' takes in a bit string 010..101 and produces a watermarked latent cube. The decoder D then produces the watermarked image, and that image is augmented. A red dashed unlocked extractor 'Ext.' recovers the bits. Dashed arrows mark the losses L_disc (image vs. watermarked image) and L_w (bit string vs. extracted bits). The bottom row, 'Finetune generative model', uses the same encoder and a locked, frozen Emb. with a fixed bit string. The flow then forks with 'or' into quantized tokens feeding an AR model, or noisy latents feeding an LDM. Both are red dashed unlocked boxes. Red dashed outlines and lock icons draw the eye to the trainable parts.
caption: Overview of \ours{}. We train a post-hoc embedder/extractor pair, where the embedder operates in the latent space (top). We may then distill the embedder into the diffusion or autoregressive model (bottom). Fig. [ref] details the distillation in the latent decoder.
abstract: Existing approaches for watermarking AI-generated images often rely on post-hoc methods applied in pixel space, introducing computational overhead and potential visual artifacts. In this work, we explore latent space watermarking and introduce DistSeal, a unified approach for latent watermarking that works across both diffusion and autoregressive models. Our approach works by training post-hoc watermarking models in the latent space of generative models. We demonstrate that these latent watermarkers can be effectively distilled either into the generative model itself or into the latent decoder, enabling in-model watermarking. The resulting latent watermarks achieve competitive robustness while offering similar imperceptibility and up to 20x speedup compared to pixel-space baselines. Our experiments further reveal that distilling latent watermarkers outperforms distilling pixel-space ones, providing a solution that is both more efficient and more robust.
